blockingIssues.description: Tests bypass CustomOAuth2UserService and CustomOidcUserService entirely by pre-creating users in the DB and injecting pre-built wrapper tokens via authentication() post-processor. The critical 'creates user on first login, reuses on returning login' logic is never exercised by any test. A regression in user provisioning would be invisible.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Rewrite tests to actually invoke the service layer: either use WireMock to mock OAuth provider endpoints and let Spring Security's full callback pipeline run, or call CustomOidcUserService/CustomOAuth2UserService directly with mock OidcUser/OAuth2User inputs to test the upsert logic.

blockingIssues.description: The 'logout_sessionInvalidated_subsequentRequestsGet401' test does not test session invalidation. It issues a plain unauthenticated request (no session involved) and asserts 401 — this would pass even if logout did nothing to the session.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: Rewrite the test: create a session (authenticate), capture the session cookie, perform logout, then re-use the original session cookie and assert 401. The current test provides no evidence that logout invalidates sessions.

blockingIssues.description: The API client (src/api/client.ts) never reads the XSRF-TOKEN cookie nor sends the X-XSRF-TOKEN header. The backend SecurityConfig uses CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse(), requiring this header on all POST/PUT/DELETE requests in OAuth2 mode. POST /api/logout returns 403, leaving the backend session alive. On page refresh, GET /api/users/me still returns 200 (session valid), silently re-authenticating the user. This breaks VAL-AUTH-007.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: In getHeaders() or in the request methods (post/put/delete), read document.cookie for 'XSRF-TOKEN=<value>' and include it as 'X-XSRF-TOKEN: <value>' header on all mutating requests.

appliedUpdates.description: Fixed stale WebSocket auth note: clarified that SSO mode uses session cookie (no X-User-Id), while fake-auth mode uses X-User-Id query param. Added OAuth2 mode activation behavior (env-var check only, no profile check). Added CSRF token requirement in OAuth2 mode.
Added note that frontend/tsconfig.app.json must exclude test files to prevent tsc -b failures in Docker builds.

Documented InMemoryClientRegistrationRepository placeholder workaround, OAuth2 success handler hardcoded redirect URL. Added Docker deployment section: nginx $host vs $http_host gotcha for OAuth2 redirect URIs, WebSocket proxy timeout, .env.example DB vars not substituted in compose.
Added docker-build, docker-up, docker-down, docker-status commands for full-stack Docker Compose operations.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add Frontend convention: All <input>, <select>, and <textarea> elements must have the hover:border-gray-400 class. All card container divs must have focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-blue-500 for keyboard accessibility. These patterns were introduced in cross-area-navigation-styling and should be followed consistently.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: cross-area-navigation-styling review: reviewer noted these patterns were applied uniformly but not documented. Without documentation, future workers creating new form fields or cards will create inconsistency.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Update the FakeAuthFilter description from 'active only when spring.profiles.active=dev and no OAuth env vars set' to 'active only when OAuth env vars (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID) are absent at startup'. The current description is out of sync with the actual implementation in SecurityConfig.isFakeAuthActive().
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: sso-auth-backend review: AGENTS.md says 'FakeAuthFilter injects a hardcoded user into SecurityContext' with profile check, but SecurityConfig.java:68 isFakeAuthActive() only checks for env vars, no profile check.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a Backend convention: In OAuth2 mode, the backend uses CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse(). All frontend POST/PUT/DELETE requests must send the X-XSRF-TOKEN header (read from the XSRF-TOKEN cookie). Frontend workers modifying or creating API client code must implement this CSRF header pattern.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: sso-auth-frontend review (blocking issue): API client missing CSRF header causes 403 on all mutations including logout. Pattern must be documented for future frontend workers.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: The skill specifies WireMock as the mandatory approach for OAuth2 testing. For Spring Boot 4.0+ projects, Spring Security Test's oauth2Login() and oidcLogin() post-processors are the idiomatic and more maintainable approach for most OAuth2 integration tests. The skill should note that Spring Security Test is preferred for testing post-authentication behavior, while WireMock (or similar) is needed specifically for testing the full OAuth2 callback pipeline (token exchange, userinfo fetch, user provisioning). The feature should distinguish these two testing needs.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: sso-auth-backend review: worker deviated from WireMock prescription citing fragility. The Spring Security Test approach is valid for testing post-auth behavior but missed the user provisioning logic. The skill should clarify which OAuth2 behaviors require which testing approach.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Step 6 (agent-browser verification) is particularly important for visual/styling features and should not be skipped. For SSO-gated features where real OAuth2 credentials are unavailable, add guidance: verify the login page UI (which is accessible without credentials), document what cannot be tested in browser (the post-auth flow), and note this explicitly in the handoff. The skill should not allow skipping agent-browser for visual features.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: sso-auth-frontend and cross-area-navigation-styling reviews: both workers skipped agent-browser verification. For sso-auth-frontend, the login page UI is verifiable without credentials. For cross-area-navigation-styling, visual consistency is the entire feature — screenshots are the most appropriate validation.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a conditional path for documentation-only features: when the feature makes no code changes (only creates/edits documentation files), skip the TDD steps and agent-browser verification. Note what tests to run (existing regression check only). The current skill procedure implies these steps are mandatory for all features, confusing workers on doc-only tasks.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: readme-documentation review: worker correctly skipped TDD and agent-browser but marked followedProcedure: true. The skill has no documented exception for doc-only work.
